svg.title: ANSI mode versus native execution on Runtime 2.0
svg.desc: A decision flowchart detailing the collision between Spark 4.x default ANSI mode and Native Execution Engine fallback on Fabric Runtime 2.0, providing guidance on choosing between correctness and vectorized speed per workload.
svg.text: ANSI Mode vs Native Execution Engine (NEE) on Runtime 2.0
The Runtime 2.0 Collision · Correctness vs C++ Vectorized Speed · Per-Workload Environment Governance · Plan Verification

g.title: Spark 4.x enables ANSI by default — Spark 4.x enables ANSI mode by default, raising errors where 3.5 returned NULL.
g.text: Spark 4.x (Runtime 2.0) ANSI Mode Default
Strict SQL standard semantics enabled out of the box in Apache Spark 4.1
Spark 3.5 (Legacy Mode)
Bad casts / 0-div return silent NULLs
Spark 4.1 (Runtime 2.0 Default)
Raises loud runtime exceptions
• `spark.sql.ansi.enabled = true` is the default property on Fabric Runtime 2.0
• Prevents silent data corruption in mission-critical dimensional models & accounting data
Runtime 2.0 Migration Impact:
• Upgrading legacy Spark 3.4/3.5 notebooks to Runtime 2.0 triggers job failures
on dirty source data that previously evaluated to NULL without failing the batch run.
Forces intentional data quality validation during ingestion.

g.title: NEE falls back under ANSI — The native execution engine falls back to JVM Spark whenever ANSI mode is on.
g.text: The Collision: NEE Falls Back to JVM Under ANSI
The Native Execution Engine (C++ Velox) does NOT execute under ANSI mode
The Silent Fallback Mechanism:
• When `spark.sql.ansi.enabled=true`, the Native Execution Engine (NEE) cannot run
• Spark transparently falls back to standard Java Virtual Machine (JVM) execution
Trap: Portal Acceleration tab shows NEE = ON, but 100% of operators execute on JVM!
Architectural Implication on Runtime 2.0:
• Untouched Runtime 2.0 environments get zero C++ Velox vectorized performance boost.
• Teams benchmark native performance and wonder why queries show no speedup.
Architects MUST choose between ANSI correctness and NEE vectorized speed!

g.title: Keep ANSI — choose correctness — Keeping ANSI prioritizes correctness guarantees over native execution speed.
g.text: STRATEGY A: KEEP ANSI (CHOOSE CORRECTNESS)
Prioritize Strict Data Integrity & Strict Schemas
• `spark.sql.ansi.enabled = true` (Accept JVM execution trade-off)
• Invalid data fails fast with precise error diagnostics and row context
• Zero silent NULL values entering downstream gold analytics tables
Ideal Workload Classes & Operational Rules:
✓ Silver Ingestion & Conforming Pipelines: Enforce data quality contracts
✓ Financial & Compliance Data: Audit correctness outweighs compute speed
✓ Structured Streaming: Streaming already runs on JVM regardless of NEE
Sizing Guidance: Size capacity nodes based on JVM Spark benchmarks.
Do not budget capacity units assuming native C++ speedups on these tables.

g.title: Disable ANSI — choose native speed — Disabling ANSI regains native execution for scan-heavy conformed workloads.
g.text: STRATEGY B: DISABLE ANSI (CHOOSE NATIVE VECTORIZED SPEED)
Unleash Native Execution Engine (C++ Velox)
• `spark.sql.ansi.enabled = false` (Unlocks full NEE hardware acceleration)
• 2x–5x faster scan, filter, join, and aggregation execution speed
• Dramatically reduces Capacity Unit (CU) consumption for big data workloads
Ideal Workload Classes & Defensive Coding:
✓ Gold Aggregations & Marts: High-volume scans over already-conformed Silver data
✓ Feature Engineering & ML Training: Massive iterative tabular scans
✓ Defensive Casting: Use explicit `try_cast()` and `try_divide()` functions
Safety Standard: Only disable ANSI over validated, pre-cleansed datasets!
Avoid disabling ANSI on raw external file landings prone to dirty type anomalies.

g.title: Decide per workload class — The choice belongs to the workload class, not to a single global setting.
g.text: 3. Decide Per Workload Class
Segment by data pipeline tier
The ANSI vs NEE decision is NOT global:
Silver Ingestion Tier:
• Set `spark.sql.ansi.enabled = true`
• Catch dirty records at the gate
Gold Analytics Tier:
• Set `spark.sql.ansi.enabled = false`
• Run at maximum C++ NEE vectorization
Architectural Principle:
A single tenant-wide default is always wrong for one
of the two workload classes. Separate them explicitly!

g.title: Record it in the Environment — Recording the decision in the Environment makes it visible and reviewable.
g.text: 4. Record in Custom Environment
Centralized Spark property governance
Store configuration in Fabric Environments:
Environment Spark Properties:
spark.native.enabled true
spark.sql.ansi.enabled false
# Runtime 2.0 (Apache Spark 4.1)
• Attach Environment to Workspace or Notebook
• Promoted via CI/CD Deployment Pipelines
100% version-controlled & auditable
Anti-Pattern:
Never set ANSI mode ad-hoc inside notebook cell #1.
Ad-hoc settings cause silent configuration drift!

g.aria-label: Then prove it in the plan
g.title: Then prove it in the plan — Plan suffixes confirm which path actually executed.
g.text: 5. Prove Execution in Physical Plan
Validate native operators via df.explain()
Confirm what actually executed on hardware:
Physical Plan Operator Signatures:
✓ FilterTransformer (C++ Native)
✓ ProjectTransformer (C++ Native)
✓ HashAggregateTransformer (Native)
✗ FilterExec / ProjectExec (JVM Fallback)
• Look for `*Transformer` suffixes in query plan
Presence of Transformer confirms C++ execution
Inspection Command:
df.explain(mode="formatted")
Check Spark Advisor UI for fallback diagnostics.
